title: Barricaded suspect killed, ending 30-hour armed standoff in east Calgary
subtitle: Suspect fired more than 100 rounds at law enforcement over the course of the incident, which began Thursday afternoon and lasted more than a day.
article: The sound of explosions and a volley of gunfire signalled the violent end of a 30-hour armed standoff in east Calgary, with a barricaded suspect killed Friday night.

The situation escalated around 8:30 p.m., causing city police and RCMP tactical officers to fire their weapons, Calgary police said in a statement early Saturday morning. The suspect was declared dead at the scene.

Throughout the ordeal, which began shortly after 3 p.m. Thursday during the execution of a search warrant , the man holed up at a home in the 300 block of Penswood Way S.E. had fired more than 100 rounds at law enforcement, police said.

No officers or bystanders were injured.

"The actions of one individual, with a history of weapons offences, put our community and our officers at substantial risk of harm," Chief Mark Neufeld said in the Calgary Police Service 's written statement.

"This is an unfortunate outcome but our top priority was always the safety of the community," he said later at a news conference. "We made every effort to bring this to a safe and peaceful conclusion and have employed numerous tactics and resources over the duration of this prolonged event."

At the time the incident ended, individuals believed to be friends and relatives of the suspect were observed near the standoff scene in an emotional state. "You've killed Pat, you've killed Pat!" someone could be heard exclaiming.
Neighbours identified the suspect as Patrick Robert Kimmel, 45, who'd been arrested for a September 2021 armed home invasion robbery in Drumheller in which no one was injured.

Those charges were stayed in May 2022 but he was convicted of a Calgary charge of possession of a loaded, prohibited or restricted firearm on Dec. 20, 2021, and given a 21⁄2-year jail term and a weapons prohibition.

The ongoing situation required many homes in the area to be evacuated and with the incident over, a number of residents were allowed to return late Friday night while others would continue to be displaced as investigators carried on with their work, police said on social media.
Memorial Drive had been closed between 52nd Street and 68th Street S.E. since Thursday afternoon, with other residential streets in Penbrooke Meadows similarly blocked off by police cruisers.

Neufeld said CPS officers demonstrated the "utmost professionalism and sound tactical judgement during a high stress and dangerous situation" while dealing with a suspect armed with high-powered weapons.
"This was a tremendously dynamic situation that posed immense risk to the surrounding community and to our officers," he said.

"I understand the stress that incidents like this can cause for residents and their families, and just know that we've taken all reasonable steps to minimize impacts and to support the community throughout this ordeal."

At this time, there is no longer a threat to public safety in the community of Penbrooke Meadows. Our members are still on scene in the 300 block of Penswood Way S.E., and will be throughout the night. The initial search warrant was related to a firearms investigation, said CPS Supt. Joe Brar earlier Friday. Members of the RCMP emergency response team were on scene assisting local police due to the "protracted" nature of the event, he added.
More than a dozen police vehicles, including tactical teams, remained in the area surrounding the house through the course of the incident.

On Thursday evening, officers could be heard trying to negotiate with the man inside the home, urging him to come out to receive medical attention or to call 911 if he was injured. A drone and a police helicopter could also be seen circling above the home.

Neighbours said it appeared police had pumped water into the basement of the suspect's home to flush Kimmel out and showed photos of Calgary Fire Department equipment a sea can parked in front of the residence.
"We could see that (police) were smoking him out, you could see huge plumes of smoke," said Justin Anderson, who lives six doors down from the suspect home and was evacuated prior to the final act.
"Police were pretty panicky - things were moving pretty quick."
Saturday morning revealed a white stucco-brick bungalow with both front basement windows blown in and the picture window shattered.
Trim or eavestrough hung limply from one corner of the structure, which was being aerated, presumably to disperse any lingering tear gas.
Police personnel examined what appeared to be at least one bullet hole in the front of the home and officers were seeking out possible damage from the suspect's rounds on nearby vehicles and houses.

The deadly encounter has been referred to the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, the province's law enforcement watchdog agency. Because of this, Calgary police won't release any additional information about the violent standoff for now, the service said.

Members of the Calgary police victim assistance support team will be in Penbrooke Meadows Saturday to offer help to anyone in the neighbourhood affected by the incident. The team can also be reached by calling 403-428-8398 or toll free at 1-888-327-7828.
With files from Michael Rodriguez and Jim Wells and Kevin Martin
